title: Hybrid tensor/pipeline sharding exploration for multi-GPU serving
content:
Status: draft - exploratory notes, experiments and TODOs

Purpose
- Capture a practical hybrid sharding approach for our serving runtime that mixes tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) for large models while keeping KV cache coherence, minimizing NCCL overhead, and enabling per-request scheduling decisions.
- Goal: reduce end-to-end latency p50/p95 for mixed small/long context workloads while keeping GPU utilization and memory usage predictable.

Assumptions and constraints - We run on multi-GPU hosts with NVLink + NVSwitch where available; some hosts are multi-socket with RDMA networks between machines.
- Models targeted: 30B-100B parameter class, FP16/4-bit quant variants.
- Serving runtime must support dynamic requests (variable prompt length) and attempt to keep KV cache warm for session locality.
- Can change kernel layout and communication scheme but cannot change model graph semantics.

Design highlights (high-level)
1) Hybrid shard layout: static TP groups inside a PP stage. We group GPUs into small TP islands (2-4 GPUs) and then compose pipeline stages across islands. This reduces per-step cross-host traffic for KV updates while preserving computation parallelism for attention kernels.
2) NCCL-aware communicator placement: create communicators at two granularities — intra-island (fast path) and inter-stage (sparser, aggregated calls). Set up NCCL with per-communicator tuning (e.g., NCCL_ALGO=ring for intra-island where PCIe/NVLink dominates, and NCCL_ALGO=tree for cross-host where latency matters).
3) KV cache sharding and consistency: shard KV by TP sub-rows (sharded per-tensor-block). Maintain lightweight directory metadata per-request to track which GPUs hold which segments. Use an LRU/TTL evict policy per-GPU.
4) Scheduler policy: runtime will choose between two execution modes per-request: low-latency (minimize cross-island communication — run on a single island and accept slower compute due to reduced parallelism) and high-throughput (spread across islands/pipeline stages). Decision based on request size, observed tail latency, and SLAs.

Detailed components
A. Physical mapping and naming
- Define island = group of adjacent GPUs that share high-bandwidth interconnect (NVLink).
- Define stage = pipeline stage composed of one or more islands.
- Each tensor is partitioned across TP ranks within an island; KV cache is partitioned by token axis across islands and within island by TP rank.

B. Communication patterns and NCCL tuning notes
- Intra-island ops: AllReduce/AllGather for TP kernel fusion (attention q/k/v matmul reductions). Use NCCL_ALGO=ring, NCCL_PROTO=LL for NVLink hosts. Set NCCL_BUFFSIZE tuned to 4–8MB for steady token sizes.
- Inter-stage ops: point-to-point scatter/gather for KV exchange, and collective AllReduce for optimizer-like reductions (rare in serving). Use NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE on cross-host links to reduce latency spikes.
- Use persistent communicators (create once at start) and reuse them to avoid startup overhead. For dynamic stage reconfiguration (rollouts), gracefully recreate communicators during low-traffic windows.
- Environment knobs to test (examples):
  - NCCL_ALGO=ring|tree
  - NCCL_PROTO=LL|SIMPLE
  - NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS|NVL|SHM
  - NCCL_BUFFSIZE=4194304
  - NCCL_THREAD_SAFE=1 (try with and without for host CPU contention)

C. KV cache layout and coherence protocol
- KV layout: for token t and head h, store K_t_h and V_t_h sharded along head and/or hidden dims inside each TP rank. This keeps per-rank memory smaller.
- Per-request directory: small metadata object (request_id -> [island_ids, token_ranges]) that lives in host memory and is replicated to the stage leader.
- Cache fill and eviction: when a request is routed to a stage, first check local KV segments; if missing, fetch from peers in the same island (fast) else fall back to inter-island fetch with batched NCCL calls.
- Consistency: serving is append-only for KV; coherence issues only when we evict/refresh segments. Eviction protocol is eventual: writeback is not necessary; we simply mark segments invalid and fetch on next access.

D. Scheduling heuristics and algorithm (runtime)
- Inputs: request.length, request.priority (SLA), recent p95 for small/large tokens, current GPU free memory, island utilization.
- Heuristics:
  - If request.length < 128 tokens -> prefer single-island mode with local KV only (low-latency).
  - If request.length >= 512 tokens -> prefer pipeline mode across islands to maximize parallelism and throughput.
  - If a session has high locality (repeated requests) -> pin session to same island to warm KV cache.
- Simple scoring function (pseudo): score(island_set) = w1*pred_latency(island_set, req_len) + w2*(1 - memory_headroom) + w3*cache_hit_rate. Choose min score.

E. Kernel and fusion considerations
- Attention kernels: fuse qkv projection, rotary/ALiBi, scaled dot-product, and softmax where possible inside island to avoid intermediate transfers.
- KV read path: implement a token-batched gather that pulls contiguous token ranges first (benefit from cache warmness). Avoid fine-grained token pulls across islands.

F. Fallback and graceful degradation
- If inter-island comms degraded (detected via NCCL errors/timeouts or elevated latencies), automatically switch to single-island policy for new requests and throttle long-running pipeline inferences.
- Expose metrics/alerts: "island_comm_retry_rate", "interstage_latency_ms", "kv_remote_fetch_rate".

Experiment plan (short-term)
- Experiment A: 2-island (2 GPUs each) vs flat 4-GPU TP across same model. Measure p50/p95 per-request for lengths 32/128/512 tokens.
- Experiment B: Vary NCCL_ALGO between ring/tree and measure p95 tail with synthetic cross-host noise (iperf).
- Experiment C: Eviction TTL tuning: TTLs = 10s, 60s, 300s and measure remote fetch rate and token-level end-to-end latency.
- Instrumentation: capture per-request timeline: enqueue->kv-check->comm->compute->response. Export to tracing pipeline.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to best assign model partitions when model has Mixture-of-Experts layers? (Do we colocate experts inside islands?)
- Cost model calibration: need to convert scoring heuristic into explicit cost units (GPU-time + comm time) using e.g., microbenchmarks.
- Interoperability with Dedicated: need to expose island topology via capacity API so customers with Dedicated pools can pin islands.

Next steps (immediate)
- Prototype communicator setup code in runtime (leader election for stage leader) — Lucas to pick up.
- Implement host-side KV directory and local fetch paths — Mei to spike.
- Build small synthetic harness for Experiment A and B — Diego to own.

Notes to self (informal)
- Avoid over-sharding: cost of remote token fetchs kills tail. Better to slightly under-shard and accept compute per GPU increase.
- Keep an eye on NCCL INFO logs; sometimes tree algorithm hides an extra hop that becomes visible under load.

References and related tickets
- See linked artifacts above. Also review: internal note "kv-cache-etching-ideas" (confluence) and PR #742 for early communicator refactor.

Appendix: quick bash examples for debug
- run NCCL debug: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=tree NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE python -m runtime.perf_test --model 33b --shard-plan ./plans/p2.json
- collect nvprof/nvmetrics while running: nsys profile -o profile1 -- python ...

End draft.
